senses.sense_definition: A child's toy consisting of vanes attached to a stick that spin like a windmill when blown on or moved through the air.

examples.text: The little boy blew gently on the colourful plastic <w>pinwheel</w> until it spun.
We bought a bright paper <w>pinwheel</w> at the seaside to place in our garden.

senses.sense_definition: A food item made of pastry, bread, or meat rolled into a spiral cylinder and sliced into discs.

examples.text: She prepared a platter of savory tortilla <w>pinwheels</w> for the afternoon picnic.
The bakery sells delicious cinnamon <w>pinwheels</w> topped with sweet vanilla glaze.

senses.sense_definition: A pastry shaped with folded corners resembling a spinning toy, typically featuring filling or jam in the center.

examples.text: The baker placed a dollop of strawberry jam in the centre of each dough <w>pinwheel</w>.
These delicate <w>pinwheels</w> are folded at the corners before being baked until golden.

senses.sense_definition: A firework designed to rotate rapidly when ignited, creating a circular shower of sparks.

examples.text: We nailed the sparkling <w>pinwheel</w> to the wooden fence and lit the fuse.
A brilliant <w>pinwheel</w> illuminated the night sky, throwing out bright golden sparks.

senses.sense_definition: A gear or wheel fitted with projecting pins or cogs instead of standard teeth.

examples.text: The watchmaker carefully cleaned the antique <w>pinwheel</w> before reassembling the clock.
Each peg on the rotating <w>pinwheel</w> tripped a small mechanical release lever.

senses.sense_definition: To spin, whirl, or rotate rapidly like a wheel, often in an uncontrollable manner.

examples.text: He slipped on the icy path and <w>pinwheeled</w> his arms wildly to stay upright.
The damaged drone began to <w>pinwheel</w> through the air before crashing into the field.
